rawFindings.title: Literal parentheses in paths cause watching an ancestor directory
rawFindings.explanation: This now treats any `(` in a path segment as a glob character. Parentheses are valid literal filename characters, so a config under a directory such as `/home/alice/project (copy)` with a watched pattern like `/home/alice/project (copy)/**/*.js` computes the base directory as `/home/alice` instead of `/home/alice/project (copy)`. Chokidar then recursively watches a much larger unrelated tree, which can exhaust watch descriptors and prevent reliable auto-watch behavior.
rawFindings.suggestion: Do not strip on a bare `(`; only strip segments containing real glob/extglob syntax, e.g. restore the previous extglob-specific replacements or require an extglob operator before `(`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Given watched pattern `/home/alice/project (copy)/**/*.js` and a home directory large enough to exceed the OS watch limit, the watcher adds `/home/alice` instead of `/home/alice/project (copy)`, causing chokidar to hit the watch limit while scanning unrelated files and auto-watch fails for the intended project files.
